# service

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/service"
```

Package service runs one service the way systemd.service(5) does (ADR 0214): Type=, the Exec\*= commands and their prefixes, the timeouts, the watchdog, Restart= and the start limiter, as typed values in a Config, driven by one actor per unit over a pure reducer.

```
start, _ := service.ParseCommand([]string{"/usr/bin/daemon", "--foreground"})
unit, err := service.NewUnit(&service.Config{
	Name:      "daemon",
	ExecStart: []service.Command{start},
	Restart:   service.RestartOnFailure,
})
err = unit.Start(ctx)      // up, or START_FAILED with its result
events, cancel := unit.Subscribe(0) // every change, never waited on
err = unit.Stop(ctx)        // ExecStop=, the signals, ExecStopPost=
```

### Directives are values

Config holds one typed field per directive; a field's zero is systemd's default, and Zero and Infinity are systemd's literal 0 and infinity. The unit-file syntax, the % specifiers, the graph between units and the actions on the system (SuccessAction=, StartLimitAction=) are the caller's. ParseCommand reads the prefixes "@-:+!|"; "+" and "!" run only where Config.AllowPrivilegedControl allows them.

### Observing a unit

Unit.State is the level — state, step, result, processes, a generation that grows with every change. Unit.Subscribe's queue is bounded and the unit never waits on it: the newest event is dropped when it is full, counted, and a consumer that sees a gap in the generations reads Unit.State.

### A daemon that forks

Type=forking adopts the daemon its command leaves through an Attacher — NewAttacher's, on Linux, darwin and the BSDs: the PID PIDFile= names, or, on Linux, with a Cgroup that lists its members (CgroupMembers), the one member whose parent is outside the cgroup (GuessMainPID=).

### The descriptor store

FileDescriptorStoreMax= keeps the descriptors a service hands with FDSTORE=1 and gives them back to its next main process, at fd 3 on with their FDNAME=; Unit.FDStore lists them. Linux only.

### One instance per connection

SpawnInstance runs a unit of a template for one accepted connection — Accept=yes —, the connection at fd 3 (LISTEN\_FDS=1), ended with its run. Not on Windows.

### The unit's control group

A Cgroup that is a CgroupUnit — proc/cgroup's group, on Linux — runs KillMode=control-group (then the default) and mixed, ExitType=cgroup, Delegate= and OOMPolicy=, every process of the unit spawned into it. NewAttacher's scope names a cgroup as /proc/\<pid>/cgroup does: proc/cgroup's Membership turns a group's directory into that path.

### Type=dbus

A Type=dbus unit is up once its main process runs and its BusName= is owned — its Config.BusWatcher, pkg/v1/proc/dbus's Conn, follows the name —, and stops when the bus announces the name lost. Linux only.

### The sandbox

ProtectSystem=, PrivateTmp=, ReadOnlyPaths=, BindPaths=, TemporaryFileSystem=, RootDirectory=, the Private…= namespaces, ProtectHostname=, NoNewPrivileges=, the capability sets, SecureBits= and SystemCallFilter= are Config fields, resolved into proc/process's Sandbox on Linux amd64 and arm64 — refused elsewhere —, added to the one Config.Spec carries. A "+" command runs unconfined, a "!" one keeps the sandbox; a start whose sandbox cannot be applied is START\_FAILED wrapping SANDBOX\_FAILED or SANDBOX\_UNAVAILABLE.

### Platforms

The reducer and every type that needs no notification run everywhere. Notifications need a NotifySource — ListenNotify on Linux and FreeBSD. Windows kills and does nothing else: a signal other than SIGKILL is refused there.

<a name="AttachScope"></a>
## type [AttachScope](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

AttachScope bounds the process an untrustworthy PID file may name: a cgroup v2 subtree and the users it may run as. It is the same type as proc/process's AttachScope, an alias of the core port's AttachValue.

```go
type AttachScope = coreproc.AttachValue
```

AttachScope is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.AttachValue`, declared as:

```go
type AttachScope struct {
	// Cgroup is a cgroup v2 path as /proc/<pid>/cgroup names it —
	// "/system.slice/web.service" —: the process must be in it or below it. Empty
	// checks no cgroup.
	Cgroup string
	// UIDs are the users the process may run as: its real and its effective uid
	// must both be one of them. Empty checks no user.
	UIDs   []int
}
```

<a name="Attacher"></a>
## type [Attacher](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

Attacher adopts a process the engine did not start: MAINPID=, PIDFile=.

```go
type Attacher = coresvc.Attacher
```

Attacher is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/service.Attacher`, declared as:

```go
type Attacher interface {
	// AttachPID adopts the live process pid, or refuses it.
	AttachPID(ctx context.Context, pid int) (coreproc.Process, error)
	// AttachPIDFile adopts the process a PID file names, read safely, or
	// refuses it.
	AttachPIDFile(ctx context.Context, path string) (coreproc.Process, error)
}
```

<a name="BusWatcher"></a>
## type [BusWatcher](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

BusWatcher follows who owns a Type=dbus unit's BusName=; pkg/v1/proc/dbus's Conn is one.

```go
type BusWatcher = coresvc.BusWatcher
```

BusWatcher is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/service.BusWatcher`, declared as:

```go
type BusWatcher interface {
	// WatchName returns a channel holding name's owner when the watch began —
	// the owner's unique name, empty for none, looked up once the bus
	// announces the name's changes to the watcher —, then the owner after each
	// change the bus announces (NameOwnerChanged), in order. It is closed when
	// ctx ends or the connection to the bus is lost; a watcher never reports a
	// lookup as a change. The engine waits for it, and for its first owner,
	// before a start's first spawn: a watcher bounds its own calls —
	// proc/dbus's wait 25 seconds at most.
	WatchName(ctx context.Context, name string) (<-chan string, error)
}
```

<a name="BusWatcher.WatchName"></a>
### func \(BusWatcher\) [WatchName](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/proc/service/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (BusWatcher) WatchName(ctx context.Context, name string) (<-chan string, error)
```

WatchName returns a channel holding name's owner when the watch began — the owner's unique name, empty for none, looked up once the bus announces the name's changes to the watcher —, then the owner after each change the bus announces (NameOwnerChanged), in order. It is closed when ctx ends or the connection to the bus is lost; a watcher never reports a lookup as a change. The engine waits for it, and for its first owner, before a start's first spawn: a watcher bounds its own calls — proc/dbus's wait 25 seconds at most.

<a name="CgroupKill"></a>
## type [CgroupKill](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

CgroupKill is the unit's control group: who belongs to it, and every process of it signalled at once.

```go

```

CgroupKill is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/service.CgroupKill`, declared as:

```go
type CgroupKill interface {
	// Contains reports whether pid is a process of the group.
	Contains(pid int) (bool, error)
	// Kill kills every process of the group at once, without a race with a
	// fork (cgroup.kill). On Linux every child later cloned into a group
	// killed this way is SIGKILLed at its fork, so the engine never calls
	// it: a unit's group is spawned into again at its next start, and its
	// kills go through Signal.
	Kill() error
	// Signal sends sig to every process of the group.
	Signal(sig coreproc.Signal) error
}
```

<a name="CgroupUnit"></a>
## type [CgroupUnit](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

CgroupUnit is the sibling of CgroupKill a unit's control group offers when it runs the cgroup modes — KillMode=control-group and mixed, ExitType=cgroup, Delegate=, OOMPolicy=; proc/cgroup's Linux group is one.

```go

```

CgroupUnit is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/service.CgroupUnit`, declared as:

```go
type CgroupUnit interface {
	// Delegate hands the group to the user uid and the group gid, -1 keeping
	// either unchanged (Delegate=).
	Delegate(uid int, gid int) error
	// DeleteBeneath removes every group beneath the group, deepest first; the
	// group itself stays.
	DeleteBeneath() error
	// Members lists the pids of the group's processes and of the groups
	// beneath it, in no promised order.
	Members() ([]int, error)
	// Path is the group's directory: the CgroupPath the engine spawns every
	// process of the unit into when its Spec names none.
	Path() string
	// SetMemoryOOMGroup writes memory.oom.group: true has the OOM killer end
	// the whole group (OOMPolicy=kill).
	SetMemoryOOMGroup(enabled bool) error
	// Stat reads the group's counters; the engine reads its memory events'
	// OOM kills.
	Stat() (coreproc.GroupStatValue, error)
	// Watch returns a channel holding the group's state, then its state after
	// each change the kernel announces, a burst coalesced into the latest; it
	// is closed when ctx ends or the group is gone.
	Watch(ctx context.Context) (<-chan coreproc.GroupEventsValue, error)
}
```

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

Config is one service unit: systemd.service(5)'s directives as typed values, the template its commands are spawned from, and the ports — the engine's configuration (ADR 0214 §9).

```go
type Config = svc.Config
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/proc/service.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config struct {
	// Spawner starts the unit's processes. Nil is proc/exec's Start.
	Spawner                     coresvc.Spawner
	// Attacher adopts a process the engine did not start: a MAINPID=, a
	// Type=forking daemon. Nil refuses every MAINPID= naming one, and
	// Type=forking.
	Attacher                    coresvc.Attacher
	// Cgroup is the unit's control group. Nil is none: NotifyAccess=exec and
	// all are refused, MAINPID= is accepted from a privileged sender only, and
	// a Type=forking unit needs PIDFile=. One that is also a
	// coresvc.CgroupMembers lets such a unit guess its main process. One that
	// is also a coresvc.CgroupUnit — proc/cgroup's Linux group — runs the
	// cgroup modes: every process is spawned into it, KillMode= defaults to
	// control-group, ExitType=cgroup, Delegate= and OOMPolicy= run, and its
	// emptying ends a unit that was up on its members alone.
	Cgroup                      coresvc.CgroupKill
	// Notify is the unit's sd_notify socket, which the unit owns and closes.
	// Nil is none: NOTIFY_SOCKET is not set, and a notify type, a watchdog or
	// a NotifyAccess= other than none is refused.
	Notify                      coresvc.NotifySource
	// BusWatcher follows who owns BusName= on the bus: a Type=dbus unit needs
	// one, which the unit watches through from its first start to Close.
	// proc/dbus's Conn is one; the caller closes it after the unit. Every other
	// type ignores it.
	BusWatcher                  coresvc.BusWatcher
	// Clock is what every wait runs on. Nil is the system clock.
	Clock                       coresvc.Clock
	// CapabilityBoundingSet is CapabilityBoundingSet=: the capabilities the
	// unit's processes keep in their bounding set, bit n capability n — every
	// other one is dropped, and cut from what root holds. Nil leaves the set as
	// inherited; systemd's "~" is the complement, the caller's to compute.
	CapabilityBoundingSet       *uint64
	// Name names the unit in its snapshots and its errors. Required.
	Name                        string
	// PIDFile is PIDFile=: for Type=forking, the absolute, clean path the daemon
	// writes its PID to, read through Attacher.AttachPIDFile once the process
	// the engine started exited — again every 100 ms, until TimeoutStartSec=,
	// while it cannot be read. Every other type ignores it, as systemd does,
	// and the engine never removes it.
	PIDFile                     string
	// BusName is BusName=: the well-known name a Type=dbus unit is up on — owned
	// once its main process runs, lost to stop it. A unit with one and no Type=
	// is Type=dbus, as systemd reads it. Every other type accepts it and does
	// not watch it: systemd adopts the owner's PID as the main process when it
	// knows none, which the engine does not (ADR 0214's S0e amendment).
	BusName                     string
	// Shell is the shell a "|" command runs through. Empty is /bin/sh: the
	// user database's shell is the caller's to look up.
	Shell                       string
	// RootDirectory is RootDirectory=: the absolute directory every command
	// pivots into (pivot_root(2)), in a mount namespace, the old root detached;
	// a command's path must then hold a '/', and lies inside it. The paths of
	// ProtectSystem=, PrivateTmp=, TemporaryFileSystem= and BindPaths='s
	// targets are beneath it; ReadOnlyPaths= and BindPaths='s sources are the
	// host's. With RootDirectoryStartOnly it is ExecStart='s alone.
	RootDirectory               string
	// Spec is the template every command is spawned from: its working
	// directory, environment, credentials, process group, limits, cgroup and
	// standard streams. Its Path and Args are the command's. With a
	// coresvc.CgroupUnit its CgroupPath is the unit's group when empty, and
	// must lie within it. Its Sandbox is the base the sandbox directives add
	// to — its namespaces, its mounts first —; a "+" command runs without any
	// sandbox, a "!" one keeps it and drops the credentials alone.
	Spec                        coreproc.Spec
	// ExecCondition is ExecCondition=: 1 to 254 skips the unit, 255 or an
	// abnormal end fails it.
	ExecCondition               []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecStartPre is ExecStartPre=.
	ExecStartPre                []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecStart is ExecStart=: one command, several for TypeOneshot, none for a
	// TypeOneshot with RemainAfterExit and an ExecStop.
	ExecStart                   []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecStartPost is ExecStartPost=.
	ExecStartPost               []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecReload is ExecReload=.
	ExecReload                  []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecReloadPost is ExecReloadPost=, after a successful reload.
	ExecReloadPost              []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecStop is ExecStop=, after a successful start only.
	ExecStop                    []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ExecStopPost is ExecStopPost=.
	ExecStopPost                []coresvc.CommandValue
	// ReadOnlyPaths is ReadOnlyPaths=: absolute paths of the host made
	// read-only, recursively, in the unit's mount namespace.
	ReadOnlyPaths               []string
	// BindPaths is BindPaths=: paths of the host bound, recursively and
	// writable, onto paths of the unit's view, which must exist.
	BindPaths                   []coresvc.BindPathValue
	// BindReadOnlyPaths is BindReadOnlyPaths=: as BindPaths, read-only.
	BindReadOnlyPaths           []coresvc.BindPathValue
	// TemporaryFileSystem is TemporaryFileSystem=: an empty tmpfs, mode 0755,
	// on each directory of the unit's view, which must exist.
	TemporaryFileSystem         []coresvc.TemporaryFileSystemValue
	// SystemCallArchitectures is SystemCallArchitectures=: "native" is the one
	// identifier taken, and only beside a SystemCallFilter=, whose filter kills
	// a call of any other ABI — x32 included — whatever this says.
	SystemCallArchitectures     []string
	// SuccessExitStatus is SuccessExitStatus=.
	SuccessExitStatus           coresvc.ExitStatusValue
	// RestartPreventExitStatus is RestartPreventExitStatus=.
	RestartPreventExitStatus    coresvc.ExitStatusValue
	// RestartForceExitStatus is RestartForceExitStatus=.
	RestartForceExitStatus      coresvc.ExitStatusValue
	// SystemCallFilter is SystemCallFilter=: a seccomp filter of named calls, an
	// allow-list, or a deny-list with Deny; a call it refuses kills the process,
	// unless SystemCallErrorNumber=. The names are taken as given: an
	// allow-list's implicit @default, as every @group, is the caller's to expand.
	SystemCallFilter            coresvc.SystemCallFilterValue
	// RestartDelay is RestartSec=; zero is 100 ms.
	RestartDelay                time.Duration
	// RestartMaxDelay is RestartMaxDelaySec=; zero is infinity.
	RestartMaxDelay             time.Duration
	// RestartRandomizedDelay is RestartRandomizedDelaySec=.
	RestartRandomizedDelay      time.Duration
	// TimeoutStart is TimeoutStartSec=; zero is 90 s, infinity for a
	// TypeOneshot.
	TimeoutStart                time.Duration
	// TimeoutStop is TimeoutStopSec=; zero is 90 s.
	TimeoutStop                 time.Duration
	// TimeoutAbort is TimeoutAbortSec=; zero is TimeoutStop.
	TimeoutAbort                time.Duration
	// RuntimeMax is RuntimeMaxSec=; zero is infinity.
	RuntimeMax                  time.Duration
	// RuntimeRandomizedExtra is RuntimeRandomizedExtraSec=.
	RuntimeRandomizedExtra      time.Duration
	// Watchdog is WatchdogSec=; zero is off.
	Watchdog                    time.Duration
	// AmbientCapabilities is AmbientCapabilities=: the capabilities raised in
	// the ambient set, bit n capability n, which a process that is not root
	// keeps across execve; they must lie within CapabilityBoundingSet=.
	AmbientCapabilities         uint64
	// StartLimitInterval is StartLimitIntervalSec=; zero is 10 s, coresvc.Zero
	// no limit, coresvc.Infinity a window that never ends.
	StartLimitInterval          time.Duration
	// StartLimitBurst is StartLimitBurst=; zero is 5.
	StartLimitBurst             int
	// RestartSteps is RestartSteps=.
	RestartSteps                int
	// FileDescriptorStoreMax is FileDescriptorStoreMax=: how many descriptors
	// FDSTORE=1 may keep in the unit's store, handed back to every ExecStart=
	// process at fd 3 on — after the sockets Spec activates, newest first —
	// and $FDSTORE set to it for every command; zero is no store. It needs
	// Notify, implies NotifyAccess=main, and is Linux's only: no other
	// platform's notify socket carries descriptors.
	FileDescriptorStoreMax      int
	// SystemCallErrorNumber is SystemCallErrorNumber=: the errno, 1 to 4095, a
	// call SystemCallFilter= refuses fails with; zero kills the process,
	// systemd's default.
	SystemCallErrorNumber       int
	// KillSignal is KillSignal=; zero is SIGTERM (SIGKILL on Windows).
	KillSignal                  coreproc.Signal
	// RestartKillSignal is RestartKillSignal=; zero is KillSignal.
	RestartKillSignal           coreproc.Signal
	// FinalKillSignal is FinalKillSignal=; zero is SIGKILL.
	FinalKillSignal             coreproc.Signal
	// WatchdogSignal is WatchdogSignal=; zero is SIGABRT (SIGKILL on Windows).
	WatchdogSignal              coreproc.Signal
	// ReloadSignal is ReloadSignal=; zero is SIGHUP.
	ReloadSignal                coreproc.Signal
	// SecureBits is SecureBits=: the securebits set, as linux/securebits.h
	// numbers them (noroot 1<<0, keep-caps 1<<4, …); zero sets none.
	SecureBits                  uint32
	// Type is Type=.
	Type                        coresvc.Type
	// Restart is Restart=.
	Restart                     coresvc.Restart
	// RestartMode is RestartMode=.
	RestartMode                 coresvc.RestartMode
	// TimeoutStartFailureMode is TimeoutStartFailureMode=.
	TimeoutStartFailureMode     coresvc.TimeoutMode
	// TimeoutStopFailureMode is TimeoutStopFailureMode=.
	TimeoutStopFailureMode      coresvc.TimeoutMode
	// NotifyAccess is NotifyAccess=.
	NotifyAccess                coresvc.NotifyAccess
	// KillMode is KillMode=; its zero is control-group with a
	// coresvc.CgroupUnit, process without (ADR 0214's S0g amendment).
	KillMode                    coresvc.KillMode
	// ExitType is ExitType=; cgroup needs a coresvc.CgroupUnit.
	ExitType                    coresvc.ExitType
	// OOMPolicy is OOMPolicy=: what an OOM kill in the cgroup does — stop by
	// default, continue under Delegate=. Continue, stop and kill need a
	// coresvc.CgroupUnit; kill sets memory.oom.group at each start.
	OOMPolicy                   coresvc.OOMPolicy
	// FileDescriptorStorePreserve is FileDescriptorStorePreserve=: when the
	// store is released — PreserveRestart once the unit rests dead with no job
	// and no restart due, PreserveNo at every end of a run, PreserveYes at
	// Close only, PreserveOnSuccess at Close or once the unit is failed for
	// good. Close releases every store.
	FileDescriptorStorePreserve coresvc.Preserve
	// SendSIGKILL is SendSIGKILL=; its default is yes.
	SendSIGKILL                 coresvc.Toggle
	// GuessMainPID is GuessMainPID=: for Type=forking without PIDFile=, the
	// main process is the one member of the Cgroup — a coresvc.CgroupMembers —
	// whose parent is not a member, when there is exactly one; no leaves the
	// main process unknown, the unit up while the cgroup has members. Every
	// other unit ignores it, as systemd does.
	GuessMainPID                coresvc.Toggle
	// ProtectSystem is ProtectSystem=: yes makes /usr read-only, and /boot and
	// /efi where they exist, full /etc too; strict is refused.
	ProtectSystem               coresvc.ProtectSystem
	// PrivateTmp is PrivateTmp=: disconnected mounts a tmpfs, mode 1777, on /tmp
	// and /var/tmp for each command; yes is refused.
	PrivateTmp                  coresvc.PrivateTmp
	// RemainAfterExit is RemainAfterExit=.
	RemainAfterExit             bool
	// SendSIGHUP is SendSIGHUP=.
	SendSIGHUP                  bool
	// SurviveFinalKillSignal is SurviveFinalKillSignal=: Close leaves the
	// unit's processes running.
	SurviveFinalKillSignal      bool
	// Delegate is Delegate=: at each start the unit's group is handed to the
	// user and the group Spec runs as, and at each end of a run the groups
	// the service made beneath it are removed. It needs a coresvc.CgroupUnit.
	Delegate                    bool
	// NoNewPrivileges is NoNewPrivileges=: no execve of the unit's processes, or
	// of theirs, gains a privilege.
	NoNewPrivileges             bool
	// PrivateUsers is PrivateUsers=: a new user namespace, its root mapped to
	// the supervisor's effective uid and gid, one id wide, unless Spec's
	// Sandbox names the maps. A supervisor that is not root implies it beside
	// any other namespace, as systemd's per-user manager does.
	PrivateUsers                bool
	// PrivateNetwork is PrivateNetwork=: a new network namespace, with a
	// loopback alone.
	PrivateNetwork              bool
	// PrivatePIDs is PrivatePIDs=: a new PID namespace, each command its PID 1;
	// /proc is not mounted again. Type=forking refuses it, as systemd does.
	PrivatePIDs                 bool
	// ProtectHostname is ProtectHostname=: a new UTS namespace — systemd's
	// private: the hostname changes there alone; filtering sethostname, as its
	// yes does, is SystemCallFilter='s.
	ProtectHostname             bool
	// PrivateIPC is PrivateIPC=: a new IPC namespace.
	PrivateIPC                  bool
	// RootDirectoryStartOnly is RootDirectoryStartOnly=: RootDirectory= reaches
	// ExecStart= alone; every other command keeps the rest of the sandbox in the
	// host's view.
	RootDirectoryStartOnly      bool
	// AllowPrivilegedControl admits the "+" and "!" commands; false refuses
	// them (PRIVILEGE_REFUSED).
	AllowPrivilegedControl      bool
}
```

Handover is what an outgoing image hands the incoming one (S0h): Freeze, Reexec, TakeHandover, Resume.

```go

```

<a name="Snapshot"></a>
## type [Snapshot](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

Snapshot is a unit at one instant: what Unit.State returns.

Snapshot is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/service.StateValue`, declared as:

```go
type Snapshot struct {
	// At is when the snapshot was published, on the unit's clock.
	At               time.Time
	// Changed is when State last changed.
	Changed          time.Time
	// Name is the unit's name.
	Name             string
	// Status is the last STATUS= the unit sent.
	Status           string
	// BusError is the last BUSERROR= the unit sent.
	BusError         string
	// VarlinkError is the last VARLINKERROR= the unit sent.
	VarlinkError     string
	// ExitStatusText is the last EXIT_STATUS= the unit sent, informative only.
	ExitStatusText   string
	// MainExit is the main process's last exit, valid when MainExited.
	MainExit         coreproc.ExitValue
	// Generation grows by one with every snapshot published; two events whose
	// generations are not consecutive have lost the ones between.
	Generation       uint64
	// Dropped is how many events the unit's subscriptions have dropped.
	Dropped          uint64
	// NotifyRefused is how many notifications were refused: an unverified or
	// unadmitted sender, a MAINPID= that could not be accepted.
	NotifyRefused    uint64
	// FDStoreRefused is how many descriptors FDSTORE=1 handed that the store
	// refused and closed: past FileDescriptorStoreMax=, or to a unit without a
	// store.
	FDStoreRefused   uint64
	// FDStoreDiscarded is how many stored descriptors were closed because the
	// unit no longer runs what stored them — another ExecStart=, user or
	// group.
	FDStoreDiscarded uint64
	// MainPID is the main process, 0 when there is none.
	MainPID          int
	// ControlPID is the command running, 0 when there is none.
	ControlPID       int
	// Errno is the last ERRNO= the unit sent.
	Errno            int
	// FDStore is how many descriptors the unit's store holds.
	FDStore          int
	// Restarts is how many automatic restarts ran since the last start the
	// caller asked for or RESTART_RESET=1.
	Restarts         uint32
	// State is where the unit stands.
	State            State
	// Sub is the step it is at.
	Sub              Sub
	// Result is why its last run ended, or ResultSuccess while it runs well.
	Result           Result
	// ReloadResult is how its last reload ended.
	ReloadResult     Result
	// NotifyAccess is the effective NotifyAccess=, NOTIFYACCESS= included.
	NotifyAccess     NotifyAccess
	// MainExited is true once the main process's exit is known.
	MainExited       bool
}
```

<a name="Unit"></a>
## type [Unit](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/proc/service/gen_facade.go>)

Unit is one service unit, driven by one actor over a pure reducer (ADR 0214 §3).

```go
type Unit = svc.Unit
```

Unit is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/proc/service.Unit`, declared as:

```go
type Unit struct{}
```

<a name="Unit.Close"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Close](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close ends the unit: the jobs canceled, the unit stopped as Stop does — unless SurviveFinalKillSignal=, which leaves its processes running —, then the actor ended, the notification socket closed and every subscription's channel closed. When ctx ends first Close returns its error and the stop goes on; a later Close waits again. Every call after Close is UNIT\_CLOSED.

<a name="Unit.FDStore"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [FDStore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) FDStore() []coresvc.StoredFDValue
```

FDStore lists the unit's descriptor store in the order the next ExecStart= receives it — newest first, as systemd hands it —, each by its name and what it refers to; the descriptors stay the unit's.

<a name="Unit.Fail"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Fail](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Fail(ctx context.Context) error
```

Fail is a failed health check: WATCHDOG=trigger from outside. The unit is aborted with WatchdogSignal= and its run ends with the result watchdog, so Restart= decides as after a missed keep-alive. It returns once the abort began; a unit not running ignores it.

<a name="Unit.Reload"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Reload](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Reload(ctx context.Context) error
```

Reload reloads an up unit — ExecReload=, the notify-reload protocol, ExecReloadPost= — and returns once it ran: nil, RELOAD\_FAILED with the result, RELOAD\_UNSUPPORTED when the unit has no mechanism, RELOAD\_FAILED naming the state when the unit is not up.

<a name="Unit.ResetFailed"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [ResetFailed](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) ResetFailed(ctx context.Context) error
```

ResetFailed is systemctl reset-failed: a failed or skipped unit is inactive again, its restart counter and its start limiter are flushed.

<a name="Unit.Restart"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Restart](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Restart(ctx context.Context) error
```

Restart stops the unit with RestartKillSignal=, then starts it, and returns as Start does. A dead unit is started. The start counts against the limiter.

<a name="Unit.Start"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Start](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Start(ctx context.Context) error
```

Start starts the unit, as systemctl start does, and returns once the start job is done: nil when the unit is up — or, for a oneshot, ran to its end, or its condition skipped it —, START\_FAILED (its result in the fields) when it failed or is restarting after a failure, START\_LIMIT\_HIT when the limiter refused it, JOB\_CANCELED when a stop replaced it. A unit up already returns nil. When ctx ends first Start returns its error and the job goes on.

<a name="Unit.State"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [State](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) State() coresvc.StateValue
```

State returns the unit's current snapshot: the level a consumer resynchronises on after a gap in its events (ADR 0214 §4).

<a name="Unit.Stop"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Stop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/unit.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Stop(ctx context.Context) error
```

Stop stops the unit, as systemctl stop does — ExecStop=, the signals, ExecStopPost= —, cancels a start running, and returns once the unit is dead. The escalation runs on the unit's own deadlines: when ctx ends first Stop returns its error and the stop goes on (ADR 0214 §7).

<a name="Unit.Subscribe"></a>
### func \(Unit\) [Subscribe](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/proc/service/observe.go>)

```go
func (*Unit) Subscribe(capacity int) (events <-chan coresvc.EventValue, cancel func())
```

Subscribe returns a channel that receives one EventValue per published snapshot, and the function that ends the subscription and closes the channel. The channel holds capacity events — 0 is 64, and the capacity is held within 1 and 4096 —, and the unit never waits on it: when it is full the newest event is dropped and counted in the unit's Dropped, and a consumer that sees two events whose generations are not consecutive reads State to resynchronise (ADR 0214 §4). The unit's end closes the channel; on a closed unit it is closed already. cancel may be called more than once.
